title: Instrumented trace propagator and anomaly bucketing for SLO attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently lack a lightweight, deterministic way to connect sampled traces to SLO signal buckets (route/model/tenant) for short-lived anomalies. Missing fields and inconsistent propagation of KV-cache and batching metadata means burn-rate math and anomaly attribution are noisy — causing false positives and noisy paging.

Goal: Add a minimal trace propagator shim and server-side span enrichers that reliably carry three pieces of information from request ingress to token-generation kernel: 1) canonical route/model id, 2) batching context (batch size, batching window), and 3) KV-cache state fingerprint. Use these fields to build an 'anomaly bucketing' layer that groups errors/latency spikes into coherent SLO-attributable buckets for burn-rate evaluation and smarter paging.

Acceptance criteria:
- Traces for sampled and synthetic requests include the three canonical attributes in a stable header/span tag.
- Anomaly bucketing service can map incoming metric/error events to SLO buckets with >95% fidelity in the canary region.
- Burn-rate alerts for the test SLO show reduced false positives in the canary by >=40% compared to baseline.
- No measurable tail-latency increase at the runtime p99 (>1ms added) and <1% CPU overhead on the inference sidecar in canary.

Design notes:
- Instrumentation: small Go shim injected at the ingress proxy (envoy filter) to canonicalize route/model/tenant IDs and compute a 64-bit KV-cache fingerprint (hash of relevant model config + key-version). Forward these as structured trace attributes (trace tags) and short headers for downstream compatibility.
- Enrichment: runtime span enrichers will add batching metadata at the batching layer (batch size, window-ms) and annotate kernel spans with cache fingerprint when a KV hit is served.
- Bucketing: a lightweight stream processor (Fluent consumer -> Kafka -> bucketing service) will join error/latency events with trace attributes to produce bucketed SLO signals, stored in the SLO signal topic for the existing burn-rate engine to consume.
- Backwards compatibility: shim will tolerate missing attributes. For older clients, the bucketing service falls back to route-only attribution and marks bucket confidence as low.

Trade-offs considered:
- Adding attributes increases trace/storage cardinality; mitigated by using concise fingerprints and marking high-cardinality fields as sampled-only for long-term retention.
- Doing enrichment in the runtime vs. ingress: chosen to add minimal payload at ingress and compute heavier annotations where context is available (runtime sidecar).

Rollout plan:
1) Implement envoy shim + runtime enrichers behind feature flag (canary region us-west-2).
2) Start synthetic probes that exercise batch sizes and cache-hit/miss scenarios to validate bucketing mapping.
3) Enable bucketing service in read-only mode to populate dashboards and compare to current burn-rate outputs for two weeks.
4) Flip bucketing as primary input to burn-rate engine for internal SLOs and monitor false-positive rates.
5) Gradual expansion to additional regions and customers.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New dashboard: 'SLO Buckets — Trace-linked' with panels for bucket count, bucket fidelity, mean latency by bucket, error ratio by bucket, and burn-rate delta vs baseline.
- Alerts: temporary internal alert when bucket confidence drops below 90% during rollout.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atl/confluence/display/OBS/Trace+Propagator+Design
- Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/2258
- Bucketing service prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/tree/feature/bucketing-proto

Notes:
- This ticket focuses on engineering the signal path and bucketing. UX for exposing bucketed SLOs in the Console will be a follow-up (PM ticket).
